title: The Briefing
tagline: AI intelligence for Gauntlet AI — May 5, 2026

items.headline: Anthropic Hits $44B ARR, Up $14B in One Month
items.summary: Anthropic crossed $44 billion in annual recurring revenue this week—a $14 billion jump in a single month. The scale of agent adoption is now outpacing traditional SaaS growth curves, with enterprise customers spending $8-$12 on services for every $1 spent on Claude software.

items.headline: Grok 4.3 Quietly Shipped with Improvements
items.summary: xAI cut Grok's API pricing, improved speed, and added stronger tool use without fanfare. While Grok still trails in reasoning (53 on Artificial Analysis vs GPT-5.5 at 60), it's useful for writing and support. For hard reasoning and multi-step execution, the pack is still ahead.

items.headline: Cloudflare & Stripe Ship Agents Protocol
items.summary: Cloudflare and Stripe released a joint protocol letting AI agents create Cloudflare accounts, register domains, and deploy live applications without human intervention. Agents can spin up infrastructure, pay for it, and ship to the internet independently. Supabase, Hugging Face, Twilio, and AgentMail are already on the protocol.

items.headline: Salesforce 'Headless 360' Exposes Entire Platform
items.summary: At Trailblazer DX, Salesforce launched 'Headless 360,' exposing their entire platform so agents like Claude Code and Codex can operate on Salesforce directly without a browser. This signals a strategic shift: when the world's largest enterprise CRM rebuilds for agents as the primary user, that's a decision about which side of the transition the company wants to be on.

items.headline: 97% of Companies Deployed Agents, Only 29% Seeing ROI
items.summary: A new Writer survey on enterprise AI adoption puts numbers on the suspected gap: nearly every company has agents running, but almost nobody sees real returns yet. 54% of C-suite say AI adoption is 'tearing their company apart,' and 29% of employees actively sabotage AI strategy. The deployment gap closed; the execution gap remains.

items.headline: Pentagon Signs AI Deals with 7 Big Tech Firms
items.summary: The Pentagon signed classified AI deals with OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, SpaceX, and Reflection AI to deploy AI on military networks. Anthropic was notably excluded after refusing to remove safety guardrails around autonomous weapons and mass surveillance. Watch how this reshapes the relationship between AI labs and the defense establishment.

items.headline: Novo Nordisk Goes All-In on OpenAI
items.summary: The world's largest pharma by market cap is integrating OpenAI across drug discovery, clinical trials, manufacturing, and commercial ops—full deployment by end of 2026. Eli Lilly signed a competing deal with Insilico Medicine in March. Big Pharma's AI arms race is real and moving faster than most expected.

items.headline: Tenex Hiring: AI Strategist, Engineers, Engagement Manager
items.summary: Tenex is building out the team behind this newsletter. Open roles: AI Strategist, Forward Deployed Engineer, Applied AI Engineer, and Engagement Manager. NY-based. Salary varies by role and experience; additional comp based on output.

items.headline: Q1 2026 Venture Funding Shattered Every Record
items.summary: Q1 2026 venture funding hit $300 billion—a record-breaking quarter. Four of the five largest rounds in history closed in 90 days: OpenAI ($122B), Anthropic ($30B), xAI ($20B), and Waymo ($16B). That's $188B to four companies, or 65% of all global venture investment for the quarter.

items.headline: Anthropic + OpenAI Stand Up AI Services Arms
items.summary: Anthropic announced a $1.05B joint venture with Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, and Goldman Sachs to help PE-backed businesses integrate Claude. OpenAI is launching a parallel structure with its own partners. The data point: customers spend $8-$12 on services per $1 spent on AI software. The labs are following the actual revenue.
